- `no-valid-values-default-applied`: nothing usable, so the default applies.
- `coerced-to-wildcard-room-cap`: the filter was widened to `'*'` to stay under
  the per-connection limit. You receive more than you asked for, never less.
- `ignored-no-sports`: options without a valid sport subscribe to nothing.
- `not-yet-available`: an event type this connection does not receive yet
  (`accepted: []`, the type in `rejectedSample`), or that is accepted and
  starts arriving once it is enabled (`accepted: [type]`).

More outcomes can be added.

rejectedSample.description: Up to 5 of the dropped values, truncated.

sport.description: Set when the entry is about one sport (a league list widened to `'*'`).

V2Subscription.description:
Opt-in subscription for raw pass-through Source API (v2) WebSocket
events. Pass on `subscribe()` to start receiving the corresponding
`<book>-v2-update` events. Omit (or set the book to `undefined`) to
receive nothing for that book — these events are opt-in only.

4casters.description:
Delivers `4casters-v2-update`. A peer-to-peer EXCHANGE: each entry is a whole
event carrying its order book, every offer with its own price and the size
left on it. Odds are AMERICAN and may carry a half point. Quoted key because
the book's name starts with a digit.

⚠️ KEEP YOUR BASE `sports`/`books` SUBSCRIPTION NARROW when you use this.
On connect the server queues the whole initial odds snapshot (~6 MB, ~3,178
games) into your socket BEFORE any v2 delivery, and a socket whose backlog
passes 8 MB is force-disconnected. Subscribing to every sport and book and
then adding a large v2 filter can cross that cap on the first sweep, so you
reconnect in a loop and receive nothing — with no error naming the cause.
Measured: `{nfl, soccer, esports, mlb}` on top of the default subscription
reconnected 18 times and received zero events; the same client with
`sports:['nfl'], books:['pinnacle']` held one connection and received
events immediately.

⚠️ PREFER PER-LEAGUE FILTERS OVER `'*'` FOR SOCCER — it is 37 leagues and
~6 MB, republished whole on a sweep. `nfl` is ~1 MB, `esports` under 1 MB.

A league only pushes while it holds a live or imminent game (30s tier);
everything else moves on a 150s sweep and only when something changed. So
subscribing to `nfl` midweek and seeing nothing is correct, not broken.

ballybet.description:
Delivers `ballybet-v2-update`. Same Kambi platform, sports and payload
shape as betrivers, with Bally Bet's own prices.

bet105.description: Delivers `bet105-v2-update`. Same Ganchrow platform as betus; a Pinnacle mirror at -105.

betrivers.description: Delivers `betrivers-v2-update`. Kambi platform; deep player props.

betus.description: Delivers `betus-v2-update`. Each `markets[].data` is a whole EVENT.

lowvig.description: Delivers `lowvig-v2-update`. Same upstream as betonline, different prices.

tippmixpro.description:
TippmixPro (Hungary, EveryMatrix). Multi-league sports need league keys
(from getTippmixproV2Leagues); nfl/ncaaf/nba/ncaab/nhl/mlb take `'*'`.
Deltas are PUSHED as upstream changes them, one market per entry.

V2Update.description: Payload of a `{book}-v2-update` WebSocket event. Two shapes exist: most books send a batch (`markets` is an array of `{ marketId, hash, kind, data }`), while fanduel, draftkings and versus send one market per event (`marketId`, `hash`, `data`, with `markets` a count). `timestamp` is epoch milliseconds on most books and an ISO string on some. Fields that differ between books are left untyped; decode `markets`, `timestamp`, `data` and `raw` accordingly.

heartbeat.description: Pinnacle: a heartbeat frame; with `matchupIds` it restates the league's full set.

matchupIds.description: Pinnacle: the league's current matchup ids. Drop any you hold that are not listed.

removedGhids.description: MyBookie: games that left the league: delete them.

removedIds.description: Ids of entries that left the league: delete them.

removedMatchupIds.description: Pinnacle: matchups that left the league: delete them.

VersusV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Versus (versus.es) v2 events.

Every versus sport is multi-league — filter by specific league keys
(from {@link OwlsInsightRest.getVersusV2Leagues }) or `'*'` for all leagues.
Only the sports listed here push `versus-v2-update` deltas; the remaining
REST-only versus sports are omitted because they never broadcast.

info.description: Generated from the Owls Insight API manifest and the owls-insight-ts SDK types. Schemas are deliberately lenient: every field is optional, enums are open (x-extensible-enum), and unknown fields may appear. Decode accordingly.
info.title: Owls Insight API

get.description:
Returns the line movement for one book, market and side of a live or recent event, from the opening line to now. The /api/v1/history endpoints cover archived games.

With neither startTime nor hours the window starts at the opening line for that book, market and side.

Snapshots whose price could not be stored accurately are excluded; the response says so rather than returning a fabricated window.

pointValue is point as a number (null when there is no point); point itself keeps the type it always had.

Pass the event's eventId field, the {sport}:{away}@{home}-{YYYYMMDD} form. The numeric id field beside it is the sportsbook's own and returns 400 here rather than an empty result.

parameters.description: Event identifier from the odds board.
parameters.name: eventId

parameters.description: Sportsbook key.
parameters.name: book

parameters.description: Market to trace.
parameters.name: market

parameters.description: Side of the market to trace.
parameters.name: side

parameters.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds to start the window at. Must not be in the future.
parameters.name: startTime

parameters.description: Look back this many hours (1 to 168). Ignored when startTime is set.
parameters.name: hours

get.summary: Returns the line movement for one book, market and side of a live or recent event, from the opening line to now. The /api/v1/history endpoints cover archived games.

Returns the odds snapshots recorded for an archived game, optionally narrowed to a book, market and side, or reduced to opening lines.

Each row is the book main line for that market and side at that moment: one line per book, market and side. Alternate rungs and team totals are not stored; a period market (first_half_h2h, first_half_spreads, first_half_totals) is stored under its own key, never under totals or spreads. Rows recorded before the one-line rule was enforced at capture, and rows from the pinnacle_mqtt source, can carry such lines under totals or spreads for some books; dataQuality.mainLineNote repeats this on every response.

inPlay is true when the game was in play when the row was captured and false when it was pre-game. It is absent when the phase was not recorded: every row captured before it was introduced, every cs2 row, and ps3838 or older pinnacle_mqtt rows.

To keep pre-game rows only, compare recordedAt against commenceTime from /history/games; where inPlay is present it is the same test as the book reported it, and is right on a delayed start where the clock alone is not.

pinnacle_mqtt and ps3838 are the real-time Pinnacle sources; pinnacle is the polled book. They are stored as separate books; pinnacle_mqtt holds tennis pre-game from 2026-09-23, from the real-time feed.

priceDecimal carries the exact upstream decimal price for decimal-native books and is null otherwise.

meta.source is archive when a completed game is served from the archive copy and live when it is read on request; the payload shape is identical either way, and meta.archiveBuiltAt says when the archive copy was built.

pointValue is point as a number (null when the market has no point); point itself keeps the type it always had.

Rows whose price could not be stored accurately are excluded; dataQuality explains the filter on every response.

A plural spelling (books, markets, sides) carrying a comma-separated list or an unknown value is not applied; it is reported in meta.ignored_params with the reason. Each filter takes one value; the singular spelling with an unknown value returns 400.

Query parameters this endpoint does not read are reported in meta.ignored_params rather than rejected; a value the endpoint read but could not apply (an unknown market, a comma list where one value is allowed, a book alias with no valid key) is reported too, with the reason in meta.ignored_reasons.

get.description:
Returns historical closing player prop lines per sportsbook from the backfill archive: the line and over/under prices at close for each player and prop type.

Historical endpoints share a per-key in-flight limit that is lower than the general concurrent-request limit. A request beyond it returns 429 with a Retry-After header giving the delay in seconds; wait that long and resend.

503 with a Retry-After header means the archive could not serve that request: the query was too expensive to run in one request, or the archive read path was busy. Wait the indicated seconds before resending; if it repeats, narrow the request with the filters this endpoint accepts.

Page one event at a time with limit and offset and stop when a page comes back shorter than limit. Do not fan out one request per book or market in parallel.

At least one of eventId, player or startDate is required; sport alone is rejected as too broad.

A player search that matches an unusually large number of distinct names is treated as a scan and served through a slower fallback with a tighter timeout.

The line and the prices live under `closing`, not at the top level of the row, and the player field is `playerName`. `opening` is present only on rows where an opening line was also captured, so treat it as optional.

A row carries EITHER a labelled pair or a single unlabelled price. `overPrice` and `underPrice` are set when the source stated which side each price belongs to. `americanPrice` is set when it published one price without naming a side. So null side prices mean the row was published one-way, NOT that the price is missing: on one NBA event of 1,133 rows, every row carried a price and 1,057 of them carried it as `americanPrice`.

Do not compare a one-way `americanPrice` against a two-way line as though they were quoted the same way. A two-way market splits its margin across both sides while a single published price carries all of it, so the one-way number reads shorter than a two-way line at a comparable number.

One row is one rung of the book ladder. `isMain` is true for the line the book was actually leading with, false for an alternate rung, and null where it is not known for that row. Null is not a hint that it was an alternate: older rows predate the distinction and it cannot be recovered, so filter on `isMain === true` when you want main lines only and expect null rows to be excluded.

An alternate rung carries one price in `americanPrice` and nothing in the side fields, and it reflects the ladder as it stood at the last pre-game capture, so it has no opening of its own. Only the main line carries open-to-close movement.

CHECK `closing.capturedAt` BEFORE TREATING THESE AS CLOSING NUMBERS. A main line is the last quote we hold with BOTH sides priced, and books commonly go one-way as tip approaches, so the two-way number can predate the game by hours. Measured on one NBA game, the median gap between the last quote of any kind and the last two-sided one was 187 minutes. The price is real, it is simply not always recent, and capturedAt is how you tell.

Pass the event's eventId field, the {sport}:{away}@{home}-{YYYYMMDD} form. The numeric id field beside it is the sportsbook's own and returns 400 here rather than an empty result.

get.description:
Returns player injury designations for a sport from two independent sources, each attributed and separately timestamped, plus a derived consensus where the sources can be matched to the same player with confidence.

Supported sports are nfl and mlb. Other sports return 404.

Every player carries one record per source that covers them, with that source own status, detail and report time. Records are never merged into one another.

record.source is a role label, either primary or secondary, and meta.sources is keyed the same way. It identifies which of the sport two feeds a record came from so you can tell them apart and prefer one consistently. It is stable if a feed is changed underneath it.

consensus is present only when the two sources can be matched to the same player with confidence. When they disagree, consensus.agreement is conflict and consensus.injuryStatus is null, and both records are returned.

Players whose identity could not be established are listed in meta.unresolvedIdentity and carry no consensus. That includes a player whose two spellings differ only by a suffix when nothing else corroborates that they are the same person, since adding a suffix to one of two players is how a league separates a shared name.

consensus.listDaysConflict is true when both sources agree a player is on an injured list but disagree about its length, for example 10 days against 60. The designation still reads as agreeing, so check this flag when the length matters.

meta.sources[source].ageSeconds is null when the age is unknown, and is never 0 as a placeholder. A source is marked stale when its age is unknown, when it is older than 30 minutes, or when it holds no records.

meta.sources[source].checks names the validations that ran on that source own data. Checks are reported per source, never pooled, so one source never inherits another.

Cleared and roster-move designations are excluded by default. Pass includeActive=true to receive them, or name them explicitly in status, which overrides the default view.

There are two clocks and they answer different questions. meta.sources[source].ageSeconds is how long ago we fetched the feed. record.reportAgeSeconds is how long ago that source published the designation itself, which is the one that tells you whether a status is current.

record.reportAgeSeconds is null when a source publishes no timestamp of its own, and is never 0 as a placeholder. player.reportAge counts how many of a player records could be dated and how many could not, so a partly dated player is visible as such.

consensus.stale is true when every dated record behind a designation is older than consensus.staleAfterSeconds, false when at least one is inside it, and null when no verdict is possible. Null is never a substitute for false.

There are two reasons stale can be null, and staleAfterSeconds tells them apart. A number beside a null stale means the rule exists but nothing carried a timestamp to judge against it. A null staleAfterSeconds means no rule applies at all, for one of four reasons: the designation is one whose currency does not decay, such as active or a status we could not map; the sources disagree about the designation; they disagree about the length of an injured list stint; or a season ending placement does not expire. The first of those covers most players on a response that includes cleared designations.

The staleness window depends on the designation, not only the sport. A weekly football designation such as questionable lapses after 10 days because the injury report is reissued every game week, while a baseball injured-list placement is given its own stint length plus two weeks, and a season-ending placement is never marked stale.

meta.reportAgeSummary describes this response. staleConsensus, freshConsensus, noVerdict and noConsensus partition the players returned and add up to count. playersWithNoDatedRecord, datedRecords and undatedRecords say how much of the whole response could be dated, and are not scoped to any of those four buckets.

A source that publishes no timestamps of its own yields no staleness verdict for a player only it covers, so filtering with source can return a page on which every consensus.stale is null.

Records are retained by the source after a season ends, so check reportedAt and reportAgeSeconds on each record.

Returns real-time Pinnacle odds for a sport. For the esports keys (cs2, lol, valorant, dota2) the response is the Pinnacle wire format unchanged and league is required; every other sport returns the normalized realtime event shape.

meta.source names the real-time feed that answered; meta.available is false and meta.freshness.stale is true whenever the response is empty.

meta.feed.lastDataAgeSeconds is the time since this sport last produced any data, or null if it never has; it is the field to watch for a feed that has stopped. For a feed that is running but hearing nothing from Pinnacle, watch meta.feed.upstreamAgeSeconds.

meta.feed.upstreamAgeSeconds is the time since Pinnacle last sent anything for this sport, and meta.feed.resubscribing is true while the feed is subscribing again after a reconnect, when some leagues can be silent. lastDataAgeSeconds stays low while Pinnacle is quiet, because the board is rewritten on a schedule either way; upstreamAgeSeconds keeps growing. Both are null when unknown, which includes every response whose meta.source is not pinnacle and the moments before the feed has received anything since it started.

Each event carries status and isLive and may carry phase: scheduled (not started), live (in play, betting open), suspended (in play, betting paused for now; its markets carry suspended: true) or closed (betting over for good; the event is sent that way for a few minutes, then removed). phase can gain values, so treat an unknown one like a missing field. When phase is present, isLive is true while in-play betting on the match is running. Without phase, isLive can be false on a match that is in progress, so check status as well, and read phase first whenever it is present.

When meta.source is pinnacle, each event also carries lastUpdate and seenAt (epoch milliseconds) and freshness: { lastUpdate, ageSeconds, stale, refreshedAt, refreshedAgeSeconds }. freshness.lastUpdate is the price change the event's freshness is measured from and ageSeconds its age; refreshedAt is the last time the feed confirmed a price on the event, changed or not, and refreshedAgeSeconds its age. stale is true when the event reads as in play and ageSeconds is over 30 or unknown; pre-match prices can sit unchanged for hours and are not flagged. The event-level lastUpdate can be older than the newest price on an in-play event, so for the age of one market read that market's last_update.

markets[].last_update is when that market's price last changed, and last_seen, where present, when the feed last confirmed it. That holds for the main lines: h2h, spreads, totals, team_totals, total_games, and their corner, first_half_ and set versions. On special_ markets folded from a sub-matchup, on btts markets and on the other markets, last_update moves with the whole matchup or sub-matchup rather than the single market, so do not read it as that market's own age.

meta.stream is { epoch, seq }, the position on the pinnacle-realtime stream that this response matches, or null when the response cannot be aligned with the stream. To follow pinnacle-realtime without gaps, wait up to 25 seconds for a frame whose stream.checkpoint is true (call at once if the frames carry no stream), then call this endpoint. If meta.stream is null, replace your board with data, apply every frame, and call again after 10, 20, 40 seconds and so on, up to every 5 minutes. If its epoch differs from the checkpoint's, or its seq is lower than the checkpoint's, call again at the next checkpoint. Otherwise replace your board with data and apply only frames with a seq above meta.stream.seq, in order; a skipped seq or a new epoch after that means calling again. The pinnacle-realtime event description has the full procedure.

When meta.stream is set, data is the board at that position after the league filter and the filters this endpoint applies to every response (confirmed finished events, events too old to still be live, duplicates), so an empty data array means no event matches, not a missing feed.

meta.freshness.droppedAsFinished and droppedAsStale count events removed because they were confirmed finished or their start time is too far past to still be live.

Esports rows each carry their own freshness; the top-level freshness is the freshest served event and stale is true only when no served event is fresh.

Prices a same game parlay on the book named in book (FanDuel, DraftKings and Hard Rock): resolves each leg to that book's own selection for one game and returns that book's own correlation-adjusted same game parlay price for exactly those legs, verified leg by leg, not a naive multiplication of the singles.

The price is the named book's own same game parlay price for exactly the legs sent, at the lines they resolved to, verified leg by leg: it is returned only when the book's answer confirms all of that; otherwise the call fails rather than returning a price. On a 200, sgp.isSGM is always true. A book whose pricing misbehaves may be paused: its builds are then a 503 SGP_BOOK_DISABLED until it is switched back on, and the other books are unaffected.

A resolved leg carries the book's own ids: fdSelection { marketId, selectionId } on FanDuel, bookSelection { marketId, selectionId } on every other book (DraftKings: its market id and selection id; Hard Rock: its market id and selection id, both strings of digits). Only one of the two is present on a leg.

FanDuel prices are FanDuel's own bet-slip price, quoted from FanDuel's New Jersey sportsbook. FanDuel runs separate markets in other states and in Ontario, so a slip placed there can show a different parlay price for the same legs. The price also moves with the market, so compare it only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt.

fdSelection.marketId is FanDuel New Jersey's id for that market. FanDuel issues a different marketId in every other state and in Ontario, while selectionId is the same everywhere, so to place a leg outside New Jersey use your region's marketId for that selectionId.

meta.timestamp and meta.resolvedAt are the same instant: when the legs were resolved against the book's catalog, BEFORE pricing. meta.catalogAgeMs is the MINIMUM age that catalog data already had then; the true age can be higher. meta.priceRequestedAt is when the price request went out and meta.pricedAt is when the book's answer came back, both on our server's clock. Each can read slightly LATER than the real moment, by the time the answer took to reach our server (typically under 100 ms). If that timing detail is unavailable, priceRequestedAt is when pricing started (earlier than the request) and pricedAt is when the answer reached our server, so the two still enclose the quote. pricedAt is never earlier than priceRequestedAt and is the quote time to use. They are present on every 200, and on a refused 422 or a no-price 503 only when the book returned a response. catalogAgeMs is omitted when the age is unknown.

422 with reasonCode "unresolved" (code repeats it) when any leg cannot be resolved on the book, including a selection the book has suspended; the legs array says which leg and why. Nothing was priced.

422 also when two legs resolve to the same selection on the book, and on FanDuel for player props whose line is carried only in the selection name, because FanDuel does not confirm that line in its price response. These are refused before pricing.

On FanDuel, alternate N-or-more strikeout rungs are priced, but its price response identifies the rung by its selection only and does not confirm its line. A 200 that includes one carries meta.lineUnverified: true and meta.lineUnverifiedLegs, the indexes of those legs in your legs array. Both keys are absent when every line was confirmed, and never appear on a DraftKings or Hard Rock build, because both confirm every line.

Player prop coverage is not uniform across books, sports and categories. The categories a player_prop leg can use on FanDuel, per sport: mlb: strikeouts, hits, total-bases, home-runs, rbis, runs, stolen-bases, singles, doubles, triples, hits-runs-rbis. nba: accepted: points, rebounds, assists, threes, steals, blocks. wnba: points, rebounds, and accepted: assists, threes, steals, blocks. nfl: touchdowns, passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, receptions, passing_tds, and accepted: first_touchdown_scorer. ncaaf, nhl, ncaab, soccer and tennis have no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused naming the markets it does post when it has not. These are not the /props categories. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: mlb, nba, wnba, nfl, ncaaf, nhl and ncaab: moneyline, spread and total; soccer and tennis: moneyline only. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

DraftKings prices are DraftKings' own same game parlay pricing, quoted from DraftKings New York (DraftKings runs separate markets in other states); the betslip may differ during a price move, so compare only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt. A resolved DraftKings leg carries bookSelection: { marketId, selectionId }, DraftKings' own ids; the eventId is DraftKings' numeric event id from /sgp/events?book=draftkings. Every spread, total and player-prop line is confirmed against DraftKings' selection data at pricing time; a line DraftKings has moved since you resolved it is a 422 line-not-echoed or line-mismatch (re-resolve and resend). DraftKings drops legs it will not combine (for example a moneyline together with the same team's spread) and prices the rest; the builder never serves that partial price: it is a 422 bet-failure whose failureCodes carry DraftKings' removal reasons in upper snake case (INCOMPATIBLE_SELECTIONS, REDUNDANT_SELECTION_REMOVED).

DraftKings prices a different set of player props from FanDuel. The categories a player_prop leg can use on DraftKings, per sport: nfl: passing_yards, receiving_yards, and accepted: receptions, rushing_yards, longest_reception, rush_attempts, pass_attempts, pass_completions, interceptions, pass_rush_yards, passing_tds, longest_rush, rush_rec_yards. mlb: accepted: doubles, rbis, runs, hits, walks, hits-runs-rbis, singles, total-bases, stolen-bases, strikeouts, hits-allowed, earned-runs. ncaaf, nba and nhl have no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused naming the markets it does post when it has not. Football categories use the /props category names (passing_yards, receptions) and baseball categories use the builder's MLB names (strikeouts, total-bases). A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl, ncaaf, mlb, nba and nhl: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

Hard Rock prices are Hard Rock Bet's own bet-slip price, quoted on its Arizona book (channel ARIZONA_ONLINE): eventId and the ids in bookSelection are the ones the Hard Rock Arizona feed (state az) serves, and a slip in another state can show a different price for the same legs. sgp.decimal is Hard Rock's own parlay price; sgp.american is that decimal expressed in American odds, rounded to a whole number the way the Hard Rock app displays it. Hard Rock game legs price at the main line only: an alternate spread or total is refused with the main line. Hard Rock confirms every line in its price response, so no Hard Rock leg is ever priced with lineUnverified. Hard Rock does not combine a moneyline with the same team's spread, or both sides of one total: it drops the leg rather than refusing the slip, and the builder never serves that partial price: the build is a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes INVALID_SELECTION and legIndex naming the dropped leg.

Hard Rock prices its own set of player props. The categories a player_prop leg can use on Hard Rock, per sport: nfl: receptions, passing_yards, and accepted: receiving_yards, rushing_yards, passing_tds, interceptions, pass_completions, pass_attempts, rush_rec_yards, touchdowns. mlb: accepted: strikeouts, hits, total-bases, rbis, home-runs, hits-runs-rbis. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused naming the markets it does post when it has not. Football categories use the /props category names (receptions, passing_yards) and baseball categories use the builder's MLB names (strikeouts, total-bases). A Hard Rock player_prop leg prices at a line Hard Rock lists for that player, including the alternate lines it publishes; a line it does not list is refused with the lines that exist. touchdowns on Hard Rock is the anytime touchdown market, taken as over 0.5. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl and mlb: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

On FanDuel, NBA and WNBA player_prop legs price the player's full-game over/under line. Quarter and alternate lines are not used, so a line that exists only as a quarter or alternate line is refused with the full-game lines that do exist.

A refused player_prop leg names the category you sent and, for a betting-name alias, the props category it stands for. The aliases: anytime_touchdown, anytime-touchdown, anytime_td, anytime-td, atd and touchdown_scorer for touchdowns; first_td and first-td for first_touchdown_scorer.

Batter props on FanDuel are yes/no N-or-more markets, exposed as the over side of N-0.5 (over 0.5 = 1+). They have no under side.

NFL touchdowns and first_touchdown_scorer are yes/no touchdown-scorer markets on FanDuel, exposed the same way: touchdowns over 0.5 is the anytime touchdown scorer, over 1.5 is 2 or more, over 2.5 is 3 or more; first_touchdown_scorer takes over 0.5. They have no under side. NFL passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, receptions and passing_tds legs price FanDuel's main line for that player; alternate lines are not used, so a line that exists only on an alternate ladder is refused with the main line that does exist.

Anytime touchdown is priced on FanDuel as touchdowns over 0.5. Hard Rock accepts touchdowns over 0.5 as its anytime touchdown market, not yet verified on a priced parlay. DraftKings does not price it yet: a touchdowns or first_touchdown_scorer leg sent to DraftKings, like any yes-only market, is refused with a 422 before pricing.

Builds can be limited per API key per minute, separately from your plan rate limit. Over that limit the call returns 429 { error, code: "SGP_RATE_LIMIT", limit, resetAt } with a Retry-After header, and the refused build does not count against your plan quota. A malformed body, an unsupported or disabled book, and a request refused by your plan rate limit or concurrent request limit do not count toward the per-minute build limit. Every other build does, including one refused afterwards: an invalid eventId (400), a game not found (404), an unresolvable leg (422), a refused parlay (422 with a reasonCode), no price (503 with reasonCode no-price) or SGP_BUSY (503).

A book outside supportedBooks is a 400 with code SGP_BOOK_UNSUPPORTED and supportedBooks, the books the builder prices. A supported book that does not price the requested sport is a 400 with code SGP_BOOK_SPORT_UNSUPPORTED and sports, the sports it does price.

503 means retry later: code SGP_BUSY when pricing capacity is reached (Retry-After: 2), SGP_BOOK_DISABLED when pricing for the requested book is paused (Retry-After: 60; a book whose pricing misbehaves may be paused this way, and a new book may be enabled for selected keys before general availability), and SGP_RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE when the build limit could not be checked. A 503 with reasonCode no-price (code no-price, Retry-After: 2) means the price request produced no usable answer: retry later. A 503 without a code is a temporary outage on our side (for example pricing, the rate limit system or subscription verification): back off and retry. The rate limit case carries limit: "system".

A build that reached pricing and returned no price is a 422 or a 503 with the same body; the status says whether to resend. 422 means the book judged the slip and refused it, or its answer did not confirm your legs as sent: the request was valid but cannot be priced as specified, so do not resend the same body unchanged. Its reasonCode is one of duplicate-selection, resp-code, leg-failure, bet-failure, bet-failure-shape, no-sgm-combination, ambiguous-combination, combined-odds-missing, single-missing, single-duplicate, single-odds-missing, runner-odds-missing, runner-odds-duplicate, runner-odds-inconsistent, not-placeable, line-not-echoed, line-mismatch, line-unexpected, line-unverifiable. 503 with reasonCode no-price (and Retry-After: 2) means no usable answer came back at all: the price request failed, timed out or was answered with something other than a price. Retry later. code repeats reasonCode on both (the SDKs expose it as the error's code), so branch on reasonCode first: no-price to retry, unresolved to fix the legs, anything else to change the slip. 502 is not used by this endpoint.

On a refused 422, reasonCode is line-mismatch when the book priced a leg at a different line than requested (re-resolve and resend), bet-failure or leg-failure when the book rejected the parlay or dropped a leg from it (the book's own codes are in failureCodes: FanDuel for example SELECTION_NOT_FOUND, DraftKings INCOMPATIBLE_SELECTIONS or REDUNDANT_SELECTION_REMOVED, Hard Rock INVALID_SELECTION), not-placeable when the book is not accepting bets on these legs (for example a suspended market), or another acceptance code when the book's response did not confirm exactly these legs. For line-mismatch and the other line-* codes, legIndex is the leg in your request and lineEchoed is the line the book priced, exactly as it sent it (null when it sent none). message is human-readable prose; match on reasonCode, legIndex, lineEchoed and failureCodes, not on message.

get.description:
Returns a sample of Stake's public bet feed: recent sportsbook bets with real stake amounts and their legs, joined to the same market and outcome ids as the Stake v2 board.

A sample, not a ledger. The source caps each query at 50 rows and gives no cursor, so completeness can never be asserted; above roughly 200 bets a minute the cap binds and the window is undersampled. Do not derive total handle from it.

Every meta key is present on every response shape. On no-data and partial-miss, timestamp, ageSeconds, hash and the bet times are null (there is no data to date) and now is the response clock; never read freshness from a null timestamp.

Every response carries meta.sampling, and sampling.complete is always false. sourceLimit is always present. On an empty response the measured fields windowSeconds and observedNewPerMinute are null; the configured fields pollIntervalMs, configuredWindowMs and configuredMaxEntries are still reported when the feed has run within the last day, and are null only when even that is unknown. observedNewPerMinute is also null on a healthy response until a rate has been measured, which is normal right after a restart.

Legs join to the Stake v2 board on outcome.id and market.id, never on fixture.id, which is a UUID in a different id space. For a fixture-level join use fixture.slug: its numeric prefix appears to be the board fixture id ("46853667-sporting-galatasaray-istanbul" matched board fixture 46853667). Verify that against your own data rather than assuming it.

Each leg carries fixture.tournament { id, name, slug, category } so a wager can be attributed to a competition without matching it to a board first. Observed on every leg sampled. There is no sport field and no tournament-to-sport lookup: category is a grouping (UEFA Champions League gives "International Clubs"), not a sport.

The feed is not filtered by sport, so bets on any sport Stake books can appear, including sports the per-sport board endpoint does not carry (cricket and handball both occur). There is no sport path segment. Any one response is a bounded rolling window of a few minutes, so a low-volume sport may be absent from it.

data[].amount and currency are null when the bettor hid their stake; payout, payoutMultiplier, potentialMultiplier and each leg's odds are nullable too. Skip those rows rather than coercing them to zero.

data[].createdAt and updatedAt pass through in the source's RFC 1123 format; the meta timestamps are ISO 8601.

Bettor identity is never included.
get.summary: Returns a sample of Stake's public bet feed: recent sportsbook bets with real stake amounts and their legs, joined to the same market and outcome ids as the Stake v2 board.

get.description:
Returns a sportsbook's native markets for a sport exactly as the source publishes them: no mapping, no team normalization, no merging. Each entry in data is one raw market blob keyed by the source's own market id.

meta.status is ok, stale, partial or no-data. It flips to stale once ageSeconds passes the book's own freshness threshold, which is set to that book's refresh cadence.

Send If-None-Match with the ETag response header, quoted exactly as received (a leading W/ is fine), to receive 304 when nothing changed. The body etag is the same value without quotes, so a bare etag never matches. A 304 on /api/v2 does not count toward your monthly quota; it still counts toward your per-minute limit and appears in your usage log. A key that has used up its monthly quota gets 429 even when the request would have been a 304.

meta.cached is false only when there is no stored board to serve (no-data, and partial-miss on the books that report it). It is not a freshness signal: read meta.ageSeconds and meta.status for that.

For a multi-league sport without league, most books return 400 with a hint to the /leagues index. Books flagged mergeWhenUnspecified instead return a merged board with league null, a leagues index attributing every market to its competition, and meta.merged true; if the merge had to truncate, meta.status is partial and meta.truncated says what was omitted.

A few books key data by event rather than by market, so one entry holds a whole game. Each book's sport set, single-league sports and league rules are in the v2Books entries of this manifest.

The SDKs expose one method per book: get<Book>V2 in TypeScript and get_<book>_v2 in Python.

The stake board is the exception to the meta shape above: it serves meta { source, cached, status, timestamp, ageSeconds, hash, now } on every response, with data as an array of fixtures. On no-data and partial-miss, timestamp, ageSeconds and hash are null because there is no board to date, and now is the response clock; never read freshness from a null timestamp.

get.summary: Returns a sportsbook's native markets for a sport exactly as the source publishes them: no mapping, no team normalization, no merging. Each entry in data is one raw market blob keyed by the source's own market id.

get.description:
Returns the league index for a sport at one book: each league key with its name and market count, for use as the league parameter on the markets endpoint.

Single-league sports still answer, with one entry.

The SDKs expose one method per book: get<Book>V2Leagues in TypeScript and get_<book>_v2_leagues in Python.
